# Reviewer memory: pod close brakes and template export

Reviewed #347 at `5dc9cc2e613a0eef60de34534e1e4a1f7fdd3b87`, one round under amended C34. The round produced four blocking findings: failed template lookup bypasses the close procedure, cached completion skips live close checks on resume, export retains dangling model relationships after a member is released, and procedure export can governance-commit out-of-tree symlink-target bytes.

## Durable review lessons

- A close stop is a one-directional BRAKE: removing it can only close more. A first-call stop test is insufficient. Test a clean first check followed by a later failed check, mutate the earlier live condition, then resume. Persisted progress is not evidence that a live safety predicate still holds.
- Keep "no procedure was declared" separate from "could not resolve the template/procedure." A null/default success-shaped answer must not make a destructive wrapper forward its request. Inspect exit status, the success envelope, and daemon-routing flags.
- An exported member subgraph must prune every relationship to absent slots, not only wiring and stage_needs. A retained reviewer's not_model_of can dangle after its author is released.
- Copying procedure assets is also a privacy boundary. Path.strip_prefix is lexical; is_dir and read dereference links. A trusted operator exporting a legitimate runtime-config symlink can accidentally publish its private target. C33 exempts hostile same-user impersonation threats, not accidental disclosure. Test only innocuous marker files, never actual credentials.
- Matched stop control passed; dropping only the stop guard made it fail. Hash pins must also be mutation-checked against an edited shipped file, not merely read.

## Operating proof and isolation

The review worktree stayed clean at the exact head. Mutations and scratch progress were confined to a plain git archive, initialized as its own repository. No GIT_* variable was exported; no dependency symlink was created. All Cargo commands used just shared-build with the canonical shared target, the normal lock, niceness 19, four jobs and the unchanged 25 GB floor. The pod HTTP target uses FakeTmux and scratch repositories; pij-tmux real-tmux tests were not run. Do not delete shared target artifacts during review cleanup.

Existing template unit tests: 4 passed. Existing pod HTTP tests: 22 passed. Dependency-free Node probes and a matched stop control passed. New negative regressions reproduced the defects. Exact-head CI supplies the local-dependency-free TS proof. Private boot/quick checks were not green: tsx, node types and Vitest were missing, and ambient Biome was incompatible; procedures, skill structure and native contracts passed.

Current C34 is one reviewer/one round; author fixes and prime range-diffs, with no second reviewer round. The old two-round memories are stale. The memory service could not update them in this session, so consult the live ruling. The deployed CLI has no pij verdict verb; use pij output verdict with the full head and --answers for a role request.

## magicWand

A procedure-backed private-review recipe that creates a plain archive, rejects inherited GIT overrides, selects dependency-free guard probes and the canonical shared target, and reports CI-versus-local proof separately. just proc listed no review procedure. This is a tooling proposal, not authorization for new work under C35.

## difficulties and encoded-proof requests

The harness caught first-call stops but lacked resumed-condition, failed-resolution and out-of-tree export cases. Preserve these regressions with the approved bug fixes. This is the highest-value improvement: future reviewers should get deterministic failures rather than reconstructing the safety chain.

The private archive could not run dependency-based sensors; do not mistake ambient tool fallback or failed dependency discovery for a code verdict. Keep the exact-head CI receipt distinct from local proof. The PRD 008 live receipt is one slot while its criterion names two plus a consulted role; PRD 010's raw-zero counter criterion must allow counted writer commits. Reconcile those notes without inventing a cost breach.
